memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'They must dedicate themselves to the Lord for the period of their dedication and must bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The previous days do not count, because they became defiled during their period of dedication.' - Num 6:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When a Nazirite's vow was interrupted, they had to start over. The previous days did not count; the period of dedication began again from the beginning. That may sound discouraging at first, but look closer — the wonderful truth is that they could begin again. The vow was not cancelled forever; it was renewed.

There is real grace in the gift of a fresh start. Many of us carry the weight of failed commitments, broken resolutions, and dedication that fell apart. We wonder if we have ruined our chances, if God is finished with us. But God is the God of new beginnings. He lets us start over.

Yes, starting over can feel humbling. The Nazirite had to begin the whole count again, and it required a fresh offering. Renewal is not always easy or painless. But it is possible, and that possibility is a mercy.

The gospel is full of fresh starts. Peter denied Jesus three times, yet Jesus restored him and recommissioned him (John 21:15-17). God's mercies are "new every morning" (Lam 3:22-23). No failure is final for the one who returns to God.

If you feel your spiritual life has stalled or collapsed, hear this: you can begin again. The past days may not count, but today can be day one of a renewed walk with God. Take up the vow of your heart afresh.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you carry the weight of a failed commitment?
- Do you believe God offers you a genuine fresh start?
- What would it mean to make today "day one" again?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are the God of new beginnings. Where I have failed, help me to start again, trusting Your fresh mercies today. Amen.
